name: Kang Yatse II
status_note: Climbed every summer (e.g. a 16-climber summit day on 1 Aug 2026, TelQuel). Inside Hemis National Park; confirm park entry and Leh district permits for foreigners before travel.
difficulty_note: Alpine PD (Wikipedia): non-technical but glaciated - scree, then a steep snow slope; 6-8 h summit push starting around midnight
base: Chilling → Markha valley → Nimaling, or Shang Sumdo → Gongmaru La
notable: Lower western summit of the Kang Yatse massif and Ladakh's most-climbed 6,000er since Stok Kangri closed; published heights 6,175-6,250 m.

name: Meru South
first_ascent_by: Japanese expedition led by Kenshiro Ohtaki (south-east ridge)
difficulty_note: Highest of Meru's summits; the 1980 south-east ridge was a long, hard line, and the east ridge was still unclimbed in 2025
notable: First Indian ascent 2 Sep 2023 by a new west-face route (team led by Umesh Zirpe).

name: Meru North
first_ascent_by: Osamu Shimada & Tamotsu Iwashima (Hida Alpine Club, Japan), 4 Oct 1980
difficulty_note: Steep north side and 800 m faces; avalanche deaths in 1986 and 1990
notable: Published heights 6,400-6,672 m; first Indian ascent 1986 (Indo-Swedish team).

base: Bhuntar → Manikaran → Barshaini → Tosh → Tos glacier (Kuta Thach base camp ~4,260 m)
name: Papsura
first_ascent_by: Geoffrey Hill & Colin Pritchard (Robert Pettigrew's British expedition), 3 Jun 1967, south-face couloir
difficulty_note: Avalanche-prone south-face couloirs, an icefall and steep rock high on the peak
notable: Local belief pairs it with Dharamsura, the 'Peak of Good': whichever looks higher shows whether evil or good prevails. A government list gives 6,440 m. First ski descent (west couloir) 2017.

name: Dharamsura
difficulty_note: Glaciated twin of Papsura; SW ridge climbed in 1977 (UIAA V+/VI)
notable: Called the 'Peak of Good' opposite Papsura; a government list gives 6,420 m.
